name: Canouan Airport
before:
Canouan's airport, and the practical way into this part of the Grenadines. It is busiest through the Caribbean winter season.

The runway is the thing that changed this island. A land reclamation and extension finished in March 2008 took it from 3,455 feet to 5,875 feet, which brought 737s and A320s within reach and opened direct access from Europe and the Americas. Before that the largest aircraft serving Canouan was an ATR 72. It is one of only two airports in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines able to take large airliners.

It handles a lot of private traffic. Luxury tourism and property drive the island's economy and Canouan is well known among private jet travellers, with a CIP lounge in the terminal.

The terminal itself is worth arriving early for. It is open air, roofed in cane palm fronds with wooden walls and columns of eucalyptus logs, built after the structures of the Taino and Arawak peoples. There are no air bridges, so boarding is on foot by airstairs.
after:
Canouan's airport, in the south west of the island.

Its runway, 1,791 metres (5,875 feet) long, is the second longest in the country after Argyle's, and it can take small passenger jets. It also handles private aircraft.

SVG Air's scheduled flights link it with St Vincent, Bequia and Union Island. Mustique Airways and SVG Air also fly charters here.

SVG Air lists daily flights to and from St Vincent, Bequia, Canouan and Union Island (and Barbados, Grenada and other islands); the Bequia Tourism Association lists scheduled flights between Bequia and Canouan. Wikipedia's current list says that as of 2025 the airport has only domestic flights; that rests on Wikipedia alone and SVG Air's list includes Barbados and Grenada among its daily points, so the text does not say either way.
